# Output

Every `--json` call prints one envelope (SKILL.md, "Output envelope").
These are the fields an agent reads most. The envelope leaves out `data`,
`page` and `error` when null and `hints` and `warnings` when empty; inside
`data` a field is there even when null unless its table says otherwise.

## Pages

`page` of every list (`find`, `lookup`, `search`, `history`, `query`, `file check`); absent from other answers.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total` | All matches. |
| `shown` | Matches on this page. |
| `limit` | The page size. |
| `offset` | Matches skipped before this page. |
| `truncated` | More pages follow. You have seen everything when it is false. |
| `next_offset` | The `--offset` of the next page, or null. |

## Hints and warnings

`hints` and `warnings` of an answer that has any.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hints[].text` | What the hint is for. |
| `hints[].command` | A command to run next, such as the next page. |
| `warnings[].code` | What the warning is about; it never changes the exit code. |
| `warnings[].message` | The warning for people. |
| `warnings[].details` | Data of the warning. |

## Entities

`graph get` shows one in `data.entity`, `graph find` a list in `data.items`, `graph neighbors` one per item in `data.items[].entity`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | The id; use it in later commands. |
| `alias` | A short readable reference, also usable in commands. |
| `type` | The type. |
| `rev` | The revision; pass it to `--expect`. |
| `record_status` | `active`, `superseded` or `retracted`. |
| `attrs` | Field values; a lifecycle state is a field too. |
| `edges[].rel` | The relation. |
| `edges[].target` | The id the edge points to. |
| `edges[].qualifiers` | Values on the edge; only when set. |
| `edges[].target_rev` | The pinned target revision; only when set. |
| `valid_from` | Start of validity; only when set (with `--full` also null). |
| `valid_to` | End of validity; only when set (with `--full` also null). |

## Entities with --full

`--full` on `get`, `find` and `neighbors` adds how each entity was stored (a field named in `--fields` shows without it). `graph history` lists the transactions of an entity for `--as-of`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `edges[].edge_id` | The edge id, for `graph unlink --edge-id`. |
| `created_at` | When the entity was created. |
| `recorded_at` | When this revision was written. |
| `tx_seq` | The transaction that wrote this revision. |
| `ontology_version` | The ontology version it was written under. |
| `content_hash` | Hash of the content. |

## Get

`graph get` adds to `data.entity`:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `current_rev` | The newest revision, also with `--rev`. |
| `superseded_by` | Ids of the entities that replace it. |
| `retracted_by` | Ids of the entities that withdrew it. |

## Lookup

`graph lookup` lists candidates in `data.items`, per given name best match first; `data.texts[]` has `text`, `total`, `exact` (the count of exact matches) and `excluded` (matches whose type cannot fill the `--for` use) per name, also for a name without match. `data.fit` is null without `--for` and `--for-source`, else names them and the fitting `types` (null: any type).

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | The given name this candidate matches. |
| `id` | The id. |
| `alias` | The alias. |
| `type` | The type. |
| `record_status` | `active`, `superseded` or `retracted`. |
| `label` | The main name. |
| `match.attr` | The field that matched. |
| `match.role` | `label`, `alt_label` or `hidden_label`. |
| `match.kind` | `exact` or `prefix`. |
| `match.value` | The matching name; null for a hidden label. |
| `match.lang` | The language tag of the matching name, or null. |
| `facts` | Null when the name has one candidate; else up to 3 links that tell the candidates apart (its parent, owner or unit): `rel`, `id`, `alias`, `label`. |

## Search

`graph search` lists suggestions in `data.items`, best match first.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | The id; check the entity with `graph get` before you use it. |
| `alias` | The alias. |
| `type` | The type. |
| `record_status` | `active`, `superseded` or `retracted`. |
| `label` | The main name, or null. |
| `match.attr` | The field of the best match. |
| `match.role` | `label`, `alt_label`, `hidden_label`, or null for other fields. |
| `match.kind` | `exact` (the whole value), `phrase` (inside it), `words` (each word in it) or `similar` (a close spelling, names and short fields only). |
| `match.score` | 100, or how close a `similar` match is, 70 to 99. |
| `match.excerpt` | The matching value or the part around the hit; null for a hidden label. |
| `match.lang` | The language tag of the matching value, or null. |
| `fields` | Every field that matched, best first. |

## History

`graph history` has `data.id`, `data.current_rev` and the revisions in `data.items`, newest first.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rev` | The revision. |
| `tx_seq` | Its transaction; `--as-of tx:<seq>` reads the graph after it. |
| `recorded_at` | When it was written. |
| `record_status` | `active`, `superseded` or `retracted` after it. |
| `command` | The command that wrote it. |
| `reason` | The reason given, or null. |
| `own_session` | True when your own session wrote it; the writer is not shown. |
| `changed` | Names, not values: `attrs`, `edges` (`added`, `removed`, `changed`) and `record`; null for the first revision. |
| `source` | Only on a revision a pipeline wrote for a source: `name`, `version` and `run` of the source run. |
| `migration` | Only on a revision an ontology release wrote: `from` and `to` (versions), `summary`, and the `renames` and `steps` that changed this entity. |

## Changes

`graph changes --since tx:<seq>` lists what changed in the whole graph after a position, oldest first, as names and ids, never values (read those with `graph get` or `graph find`). `data.items` has one entry per transaction in which you see a change.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `since` | The position asked for, as `tx:<seq>` (or with an entity id). |
| `since_tx_id` | The id of that transaction, null for `tx:0`. A stored `next_tx_id` that differs from it means the log you read is gone: start again from `tx:0`. |
| `head` | The graph's seq. |
| `next` | The position after this page: the `--since` of the next call. |
| `next_tx_id` | The id of the transaction `next` names, null for `tx:0`. |
| `more` | True when another call may return more. A page can be empty and still have `more`; you are up to date when it is false. |
| `view` | Null without a read limit, else a digest of what you may see; start again from `tx:0` when it differs from the one you stored. |
| `items` | The transactions, oldest first. |
| `items[].tx_seq` | The transaction's seq. |
| `items[].tx_id` | Its id. |
| `items[].recorded_at` | When it was written. |
| `items[].command` | The command that wrote it. |
| `items[].reason` | The reason given, or null. |
| `items[].own_session` | True when your own session wrote it. |
| `items[].action` | Only on a write by `do`: `name` and `hash` of the action. |
| `items[].source` | Only on a write for a source: `name`, `version` and `run` of the source run. |
| `items[].migration` | Only on a data migration of an ontology release: `from`, `to` (versions) and `summary`. Re-read what you hold: names may have changed and an entity may have left your view. |
| `items[].partial` | True when the transaction goes on on the next page. |
| `items[].entities` | The entities it changed that you see. |
| `items[].entities[].id` | The id. |
| `items[].entities[].type` | The type. |
| `items[].entities[].rev` | The revision; 1 is the creation. |
| `items[].entities[].record_status` | `active`, `superseded` or `retracted`. |
| `items[].entities[].changed` | Names, not values, as in History; null for the first revision. |
| `items[].entities[].targets` | Ids of the entities at the other end of the relations this revision added, removed or changed; their view changed too. |
| `items[].entities[].targets_more` | Only with more than 50 targets: how many more. |

## Write results

`data` of a write; `graph apply` has one per document in `data.results[].result`. Error findings refuse the write and come in `error.details.findings`; warning findings ride along here.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `tx_id` | The transaction id; null on a dry run or when nothing changed. |
| `seq` | The graph's seq after the write; null on a dry run or when nothing changed. |
| `event_id` | The audit event; null on a dry run or when nothing changed. |
| `dry_run` | True when nothing was written. |
| `idempotent_replay` | True when a retry returned the first result. |
| `id` | The id when one entity was written, else null. |
| `version` | Its new `rev` when one entity was written, else null. |
| `entity_count` | How many entities were written. |
| `entities[].id` | Each entity written; null for a create on a dry run. |
| `entities[].alias` | Its alias. |
| `entities[].rev` | Its new revision; the current one when it is unchanged. |
| `entities[].changed` | False when the write left it as it was (no new revision). |
| `entities[].type` | Its type. |
| `entities[].ops` | The operations that touched it. |
| `entities[].local` | Its `local` name from a change set, or null. |
| `entities` | Null with `graph apply --summary`. |
| `reconcile` | Only for a reconcile document: its `source` and, per scope, the counts (`created`, `updated`, `unchanged`, `moved`, `adopted`, `kept`, `retired`, `revived`) and `retired_keys`: all of them on a dry run, at most 20 when written. |
| `findings` | Warnings about the written data: `severity`, `code`, `message`. |
